subject: snail
pitch: A garden snail on an adventure. A glossy spiral shell striped in caramel, chocolate and cream, a soft grey-green body with a pebbly texture and a slimy shine, two long eye stalks with little black eyes and two short feelers below. A tiny ladybird hitches a ride on top of the shell.
reasoning:
I need to stick to only the documented SDK functions I know about—things like builder creation, joints, chains, sweeps, parts, lathes, extrusions, decals, and the various painting and geometry helpers—rather than guessing at undocumented APIs.

For the shell, lathe is risky since its outline format is unclear, so I'm leaning toward building it from primitives instead: a scaled sphere for the main body plus decreasing spheres and tori arranged diagonally to suggest a spiral whorl pattern, which gives a stylized shell look. For the body, I'm considering capsule geometry, though I'm unsure if that's a supported shape either.

For texture, I'll use surface scatter to place small pebble-like spheres across the body, using the documented surface and stick APIs rather than guessing at risky functions. Eye stalks and feelers get built with joints and sweeps, with sphere eyeballs and black pupils at the tips. For a ladybird variant, I'm planning a red sphere body, black head, and black spots placed using surface hit points.

I'm now working out real-world scale: garden snails run about 3-5cm, so I'm sizing the shell around 4.5cm radius and the body length around 12cm, with eye stalks rising to roughly 11cm, orienting the whole model to face forward along +Z with the head at the front and the body sweeping from near the ground up toward the shell.

Now I'm placing the head joint and building eye stalks as curved chains ending in small black eyeballs with white highlights, adding thin feelers near the head, and figuring out the shell as layered tori of decreasing radius stacked to mimic a spiral, needing to tilt them properly so they rest naturally on the snail's back instead of lying flat.

I think a cleaner approach is a scaled sphere as the shell's main dome, with banded tori in chocolate and cream at different latitudes oriented along a backward-up axis, plus a small cone tip for the spire -- giving a glossy striped shell look without overcomplicating the geometry.

For the ladybird sitting on top, I'm placing a small flattened red body sphere near the shell's peak with a tiny black head sphere at the front, then computing spot positions geometrically as offsets on the ellipsoid surface using the half-axis formula so each black spot sits flush on the curved body rather than floating above it.

For the pebbly texture, I'm scattering small bump spheres along the body's sweep path, computing each point's position from a radius and angle around the tube cross-section so they land on the upper visible surface, and deciding to skip explicit chain binding for stalks since an unbound sweep will just default to the nearest joint.

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy: a root-level body joint, a head joint parented to body, and a shell joint also parented to body, using the parent option to establish these relationships, then adding a bug joint for the ladybird positioned relative to the shell. I'm defining a color palette with hex values for caramel, chocolate, cream, and body tones to use across the sweeps and materials.

I'm sketching out the body shape as a sweep along a curved path with a slight taper toward the head, capped with a small sphere where the head meets, then building the shell as a scaled sphere with a small spire cone on top. For the shell's spiral banding, I'm rotating torus geometries so they lie flat as horizontal rings around the ellipsoid shell, computing each ring's radius from the sphere's curvature at different heights and alternating between chocolate and cream colors to suggest a spiral pattern.

For the eyes, I'm building thin stalk sweeps extending up from the head with small black spheres at the tips and tiny white highlights for glints, plus shorter feeler sweeps near the base of the stalks. I'm scattering small pebble-like spheres across the body's surface using a seeded random function to vary size and placement, and adding a pale flattened sphere as a subtle shine highlight on the body's back.

For the ladybird, I'm placing a scaled red sphere on the shell with a small black head sphere and four black spot spheres positioned using the ellipsoid's surface curvature so they sit flush against the body. I'm double-checking that the body's lowest point clears the ground, then finishing with the part-placement calls referencing the joints and colors, and wrapping everything in a builder call with the model's name for the export metadata.
